# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1342
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1342
- **Title**: fix(1334): prune skill directories the seed retirement leaves empty
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1334-skills-empty-dirs` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +87
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T19:54:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:30:34Z

## PR Description

## Root cause

Not a sync/materialization bug — the dirs are **deliberate leftovers of the skills retirement** (gh-1164 / #1151, shipped in v1.0.511+): on launch the app removes app-seeded `SKILL.md` copies that byte-match the retired fingerprints (`create-goal`, `fa-self-config`, js-apps per-platform variants) **but leaves their directories behind**. A device upgraded from a pre-#1151 build ends up with exactly three empty dirs under `.fah/skills/` — the filed symptom. They are invisible to discovery (builtins still serve from the package), but glaringly visible to an exploring agent: `ls .fah/skills/` shows skill names with no bodies, reading as "directories created, file writes skipped". Combined with agent memory still referencing the old `.fah/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` paths, the session concluded skills were broken. `.fah/widget-sources/` is unrelated: it is materialized on demand by the `apps_catalog` tool.

## Fix

`_seedBundledSkills` (flutter_app) collapses its two duplicate retire loops into one `_retireSeededCopy` helper that, after removing a retired `SKILL.md`, **also removes the skill directory when it is left empty**:

- dir with a surviving user file (script/notes dropped next to a seed) stays — the review -HUjo guarantee holds;
- a customized copy (byte-mismatch = user override) is never touched;
- the empty-dir prune also fires when the copy is **already gone**, so devices already on 1.0.519/520 — the filed field state — repair on their next launch without a reinstall;
- missing dirs are a no-op (fresh installs never see ghost dirs).

Skill bodies themselves stay package-served by design (#1151/gh-1164): the system prompt advertises `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and the `read` tool serves the embedded copy with zero filesystem access (core, host-independent — regression-pinned by `test/skills/builtin_skills_test.dart`). No re-seeding to disk: that would resurrect the exact drift/shadowing the retirement killed (on-disk copies shadow builtins in discovery precedence).

## Delivered vs remaining

- Delivered: ghost empty skill dirs pruned (incl. already-ghosted devices, next launch); user files/overrides untouched; regression test `upgrade path prunes skill directories the cleanup empties` covering prune-on-remove, repair-already-empty (the filed device state), user-file survival, plus an end-to-end `read builtin://skills/js-apps/SKILL.md` through the real read tool on the mobile-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`.
- Remaining (by design, not this bug): builtins are intentionally not materialized to `.fah/skills/<name>/` on disk; agents should follow the prompt's `builtin://` locations. The iOS WASI shell `ls`/`cat` visibility split is #1335 (separate seam — the `read` tool path is env-free and unaffected).

## Verification (honest disclosure)

- System dart/flutter on this box is machine-guarded (EPERM/137, known); verified via temp Flutter SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, Dart 3.x) + fleet pub cache + `BOT=false` + CI-style placeholder `.env`.
- RED→GREEN: the new test reproduced the exact filed state first (`.fah/skills` = `['create-goal','fa-self-config','js-apps']` empty dirs), then passed after the fix.
- `flutter test test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart` → 15/15 (all pre-existing #1151/gh-1164 pins hold); `dart analyze` on the two changed files → clean (one pre-existing `unused_import` warning on pristine main, untouched); `dart format` clean.
- Not verified on a real device (no simulator here): acceptance is CI + post-merge. Exact device repro for QA: install ≤1.0.510 → seed skills → upgrade to a build with this fix → launch once → Files view / agent `ls .fah/skills/` shows no empty `js-apps/`, `create-goal/`, `fa-self-config/` dirs; agent `read` of each prompt-advertised `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` returns the body.

Fixes #1334

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1342
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1342
- **Title**: fix(1334): prune skill directories the seed retirement leaves empty
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1334-skills-empty-dirs` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +87
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T19:54:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:30:34Z

## PR Description

## Root cause

Not a sync/materialization bug — the dirs are **deliberate leftovers of the skills retirement** (gh-1164 / #1151, shipped in v1.0.511+): on launch the app removes app-seeded `SKILL.md` copies that byte-match the retired fingerprints (`create-goal`, `fa-self-config`, js-apps per-platform variants) **but leaves their directories behind**. A device upgraded from a pre-#1151 build ends up with exactly three empty dirs under `.fah/skills/` — the filed symptom. They are invisible to discovery (builtins still serve from the package), but glaringly visible to an exploring agent: `ls .fah/skills/` shows skill names with no bodies, reading as "directories created, file writes skipped". Combined with agent memory still referencing the old `.fah/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` paths, the session concluded skills were broken. `.fah/widget-sources/` is unrelated: it is materialized on demand by the `apps_catalog` tool.

## Fix

`_seedBundledSkills` (flutter_app) collapses its two duplicate retire loops into one `_retireSeededCopy` helper that, after removing a retired `SKILL.md`, **also removes the skill directory when it is left empty**:

- dir with a surviving user file (script/notes dropped next to a seed) stays — the review -HUjo guarantee holds;
- a customized copy (byte-mismatch = user override) is never touched;
- the empty-dir prune also fires when the copy is **already gone**, so devices already on 1.0.519/520 — the filed field state — repair on their next launch without a reinstall;
- missing dirs are a no-op (fresh installs never see ghost dirs).

Skill bodies themselves stay package-served by design (#1151/gh-1164): the system prompt advertises `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and the `read` tool serves the embedded copy with zero filesystem access (core, host-independent — regression-pinned by `test/skills/builtin_skills_test.dart`). No re-seeding to disk: that would resurrect the exact drift/shadowing the retirement killed (on-disk copies shadow builtins in discovery precedence).

## Delivered vs remaining

- Delivered: ghost empty skill dirs pruned (incl. already-ghosted devices, next launch); user files/overrides untouched; regression test `upgrade path prunes skill directories the cleanup empties` covering prune-on-remove, repair-already-empty (the filed device state), user-file survival, plus an end-to-end `read builtin://skills/js-apps/SKILL.md` through the real read tool on the mobile-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`.
- Remaining (by design, not this bug): builtins are intentionally not materialized to `.fah/skills/<name>/` on disk; agents should follow the prompt's `builtin://` locations. The iOS WASI shell `ls`/`cat` visibility split is #1335 (separate seam — the `read` tool path is env-free and unaffected).

## Verification (honest disclosure)

- System dart/flutter on this box is machine-guarded (EPERM/137, known); verified via temp Flutter SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, Dart 3.x) + fleet pub cache + `BOT=false` + CI-style placeholder `.env`.
- RED→GREEN: the new test reproduced the exact filed state first (`.fah/skills` = `['create-goal','fa-self-config','js-apps']` empty dirs), then passed after the fix.
- `flutter test test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart` → 15/15 (all pre-existing #1151/gh-1164 pins hold); `dart analyze` on the two changed files → clean (one pre-existing `unused_import` warning on pristine main, untouched); `dart format` clean.
- Not verified on a real device (no simulator here): acceptance is CI + post-merge. Exact device repro for QA: install ≤1.0.510 → seed skills → upgrade to a build with this fix → launch once → Files view / agent `ls .fah/skills/` shows no empty `js-apps/`, `create-goal/`, `fa-self-config/` dirs; agent `read` of each prompt-advertised `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` returns the body.

Fixes #1334

Not a sync/materialization bug — the dirs are **deliberate leftovers of the skills retirement** (gh-1164 / #1151, shipped in v1.0.511+): on launch the app removes app-seeded `SKILL.md` copies that byte-match the retired fingerprints (`create-goal`, `fa-self-config`, js-apps per-platform variants) **but leaves their directories behind**. A device upgraded from a pre-#1151 build ends up with exactly three empty dirs under `.fah/skills/` — the filed symptom. They are invisible to discovery (builtins still serve from the package), but glaringly visible to an exploring agent: `ls .fah/skills/` shows skill names with no bodies, reading as "directories created, file writes skipped". Combined with agent memory still referencing the old `.fah/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` paths, the session concluded skills were broken. `.fah/widget-sources/` is unrelated: it is materialized on demand by the `apps_catalog` tool.

## Fix

`_seedBundledSkills` (flutter_app) collapses its two duplicate retire loops into one `_retireSeededCopy` helper that, after removing a retired `SKILL.md`, **also removes the skill directory when it is left empty**:

- dir with a surviving user file (script/notes dropped next to a seed) stays — the review -HUjo guarantee holds;
- a customized copy (byte-mismatch = user override) is never touched;
- the empty-dir prune also fires when the copy is **already gone**, so devices already on 1.0.519/520 — the filed field state — repair on their next launch without a reinstall;
- missing dirs are a no-op (fresh installs never see ghost dirs).

Skill bodies themselves stay package-served by design (#1151/gh-1164): the system prompt advertises `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and the `read` tool serves the embedded copy with zero filesystem access (core, host-independent — regression-pinned by `test/skills/builtin_skills_test.dart`). No re-seeding to disk: that would resurrect the exact drift/shadowing the retirement killed (on-disk copies shadow builtins in discovery precedence).

## Delivered vs remaining

- Delivered: ghost empty skill dirs pruned (incl. already-ghosted devices, next launch); user files/overrides untouched; regression test `upgrade path prunes skill directories the cleanup empties` covering prune-on-remove, repair-already-empty (the filed device state), user-file survival, plus an end-to-end `read builtin://skills/js-apps/SKILL.md` through the real read tool on the mobile-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`.
- Remaining (by design, not this bug): builtins are intentionally not materialized to `.fah/skills/<name>/` on disk; agents should follow the prompt's `builtin://` locations. The iOS WASI shell `ls`/`cat` visibility split is #1335 (separate seam — the `read` tool path is env-free and unaffected).

## Verification (honest disclosure)

- System dart/flutter on this box is machine-guarded (EPERM/137, known); verified via temp Flutter SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, Dart 3.x) + fleet pub cache + `BOT=false` + CI-style placeholder `.env`.
- RED→GREEN: the new test reproduced the exact filed state first (`.fah/skills` = `['create-goal','fa-self-config','js-apps']` empty dirs), then passed after the fix.
- `flutter test test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart` → 15/15 (all pre-existing #1151/gh-1164 pins hold); `dart analyze` on the two changed files → clean (one pre-existing `unused_import` warning on pristine main, untouched); `dart format` clean.
- Not verified on a real device (no simulator here): acceptance is CI + post-merge. Exact device repro for QA: install ≤1.0.510 → seed skills → upgrade to a build with this fix → launch once → Files view / agent `ls .fah/skills/` shows no empty `js-apps/`, `create-goal/`, `fa-self-config/` dirs; agent `read` of each prompt-advertised `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` returns the body.

Fixes #1334

- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:30:34Z

## PR Description

## Root cause

Not a sync/materialization bug — the dirs are **deliberate leftovers of the skills retirement** (gh-1164 / #1151, shipped in v1.0.511+): on launch the app removes app-seeded `SKILL.md` copies that byte-match the retired fingerprints (`create-goal`, `fa-self-config`, js-apps per-platform variants) **but leaves their directories behind**. A device upgraded from a pre-#1151 build ends up with exactly three empty dirs under `.fah/skills/` — the filed symptom. They are invisible to discovery (builtins still serve from the package), but glaringly visible to an exploring agent: `ls .fah/skills/` shows skill names with no bodies, reading as "directories created, file writes skipped". Combined with agent memory still referencing the old `.fah/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` paths, the session concluded skills were broken. `.fah/widget-sources/` is unrelated: it is materialized on demand by the `apps_catalog` tool.

## Fix

`_seedBundledSkills` (flutter_app) collapses its two duplicate retire loops into one `_retireSeededCopy` helper that, after removing a retired `SKILL.md`, **also removes the skill directory when it is left empty**:

- dir with a surviving user file (script/notes dropped next to a seed) stays — the review -HUjo guarantee holds;
- a customized copy (byte-mismatch = user override) is never touched;
- the empty-dir prune also fires when the copy is **already gone**, so devices already on 1.0.519/520 — the filed field state — repair on their next launch without a reinstall;
- missing dirs are a no-op (fresh installs never see ghost dirs).

Skill bodies themselves stay package-served by design (#1151/gh-1164): the system prompt advertises `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and the `read` tool serves the embedded copy with zero filesystem access (core, host-independent — regression-pinned by `test/skills/builtin_skills_test.dart`). No re-seeding to disk: that would resurrect the exact drift/shadowing the retirement killed (on-disk copies shadow builtins in discovery precedence).

## Delivered vs remaining

- Delivered: ghost empty skill dirs pruned (incl. already-ghosted devices, next launch); user files/overrides untouched; regression test `upgrade path prunes skill directories the cleanup empties` covering prune-on-remove, repair-already-empty (the filed device state), user-file survival, plus an end-to-end `read builtin://skills/js-apps/SKILL.md` through the real read tool on the mobile-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`.
- Remaining (by design, not this bug): builtins are intentionally not materialized to `.fah/skills/<name>/` on disk; agents should follow the prompt's `builtin://` locations. The iOS WASI shell `ls`/`cat` visibility split is #1335 (separate seam — the `read` tool path is env-free and unaffected).

## Verification (honest disclosure)

- System dart/flutter on this box is machine-guarded (EPERM/137, known); verified via temp Flutter SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, Dart 3.x) + fleet pub cache + `BOT=false` + CI-style placeholder `.env`.
- RED→GREEN: the new test reproduced the exact filed state first (`.fah/skills` = `['create-goal','fa-self-config','js-apps']` empty dirs), then passed after the fix.
- `flutter test test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart` → 15/15 (all pre-existing #1151/gh-1164 pins hold); `dart analyze` on the two changed files → clean (one pre-existing `unused_import` warning on pristine main, untouched); `dart format` clean.
- Not verified on a real device (no simulator here): acceptance is CI + post-merge. Exact device repro for QA: install ≤1.0.510 → seed skills → upgrade to a build with this fix → launch once → Files view / agent `ls .fah/skills/` shows no empty `js-apps/`, `create-goal/`, `fa-self-config/` dirs; agent `read` of each prompt-advertised `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` returns the body.

Fixes #1334

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1342
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1342
- **Title**: fix(1334): prune skill directories the seed retirement leaves empty
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1334-skills-empty-dirs` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +87
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T19:54:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:30:34Z

## PR Description

## Root cause

Not a sync/materialization bug — the dirs are **deliberate leftovers of the skills retirement** (gh-1164 / #1151, shipped in v1.0.511+): on launch the app removes app-seeded `SKILL.md` copies that byte-match the retired fingerprints (`create-goal`, `fa-self-config`, js-apps per-platform variants) **but leaves their directories behind**. A device upgraded from a pre-#1151 build ends up with exactly three empty dirs under `.fah/skills/` — the filed symptom. They are invisible to discovery (builtins still serve from the package), but glaringly visible to an exploring agent: `ls .fah/skills/` shows skill names with no bodies, reading as "directories created, file writes skipped". Combined with agent memory still referencing the old `.fah/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` paths, the session concluded skills were broken. `.fah/widget-sources/` is unrelated: it is materialized on demand by the `apps_catalog` tool.

## Fix

`_seedBundledSkills` (flutter_app) collapses its two duplicate retire loops into one `_retireSeededCopy` helper that, after removing a retired `SKILL.md`, **also removes the skill directory when it is left empty**:

- dir with a surviving user file (script/notes dropped next to a seed) stays — the review -HUjo guarantee holds;
- a customized copy (byte-mismatch = user override) is never touched;
- the empty-dir prune also fires when the copy is **already gone**, so devices already on 1.0.519/520 — the filed field state — repair on their next launch without a reinstall;
- missing dirs are a no-op (fresh installs never see ghost dirs).

Skill bodies themselves stay package-served by design (#1151/gh-1164): the system prompt advertises `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and the `read` tool serves the embedded copy with zero filesystem access (core, host-independent — regression-pinned by `test/skills/builtin_skills_test.dart`). No re-seeding to disk: that would resurrect the exact drift/shadowing the retirement killed (on-disk copies shadow builtins in discovery precedence).

## Delivered vs remaining

- Delivered: ghost empty skill dirs pruned (incl. already-ghosted devices, next launch); user files/overrides untouched; regression test `upgrade path prunes skill directories the cleanup empties` covering prune-on-remove, repair-already-empty (the filed device state), user-file survival, plus an end-to-end `read builtin://skills/js-apps/SKILL.md` through the real read tool on the mobile-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`.
- Remaining (by design, not this bug): builtins are intentionally not materialized to `.fah/skills/<name>/` on disk; agents should follow the prompt's `builtin://` locations. The iOS WASI shell `ls`/`cat` visibility split is #1335 (separate seam — the `read` tool path is env-free and unaffected).

## Verification (honest disclosure)

- System dart/flutter on this box is machine-guarded (EPERM/137, known); verified via temp Flutter SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, Dart 3.x) + fleet pub cache + `BOT=false` + CI-style placeholder `.env`.
- RED→GREEN: the new test reproduced the exact filed state first (`.fah/skills` = `['create-goal','fa-self-config','js-apps']` empty dirs), then passed after the fix.
- `flutter test test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart` → 15/15 (all pre-existing #1151/gh-1164 pins hold); `dart analyze` on the two changed files → clean (one pre-existing `unused_import` warning on pristine main, untouched); `dart format` clean.
- Not verified on a real device (no simulator here): acceptance is CI + post-merge. Exact device repro for QA: install ≤1.0.510 → seed skills → upgrade to a build with this fix → launch once → Files view / agent `ls .fah/skills/` shows no empty `js-apps/`, `create-goal/`, `fa-self-config/` dirs; agent `read` of each prompt-advertised `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` returns the body.

Fixes #1334

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1342
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1342
- **Title**: fix(1334): prune skill directories the seed retirement leaves empty
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1334-skills-empty-dirs` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +87
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T19:54:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:30:34Z

## PR Description

## Root cause

Not a sync/materialization bug — the dirs are **deliberate leftovers of the skills retirement** (gh-1164 / #1151, shipped in v1.0.511+): on launch the app removes app-seeded `SKILL.md` copies that byte-match the retired fingerprints (`create-goal`, `fa-self-config`, js-apps per-platform variants) **but leaves their directories behind**. A device upgraded from a pre-#1151 build ends up with exactly three empty dirs under `.fah/skills/` — the filed symptom. They are invisible to discovery (builtins still serve from the package), but glaringly visible to an exploring agent: `ls .fah/skills/` shows skill names with no bodies, reading as "directories created, file writes skipped". Combined with agent memory still referencing the old `.fah/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` paths, the session concluded skills were broken. `.fah/widget-sources/` is unrelated: it is materialized on demand by the `apps_catalog` tool.

## Fix

`_seedBundledSkills` (flutter_app) collapses its two duplicate retire loops into one `_retireSeededCopy` helper that, after removing a retired `SKILL.md`, **also removes the skill directory when it is left empty**:

- dir with a surviving user file (script/notes dropped next to a seed) stays — the review -HUjo guarantee holds;
- a customized copy (byte-mismatch = user override) is never touched;
- the empty-dir prune also fires when the copy is **already gone**, so devices already on 1.0.519/520 — the filed field state — repair on their next launch without a reinstall;
- missing dirs are a no-op (fresh installs never see ghost dirs).

Skill bodies themselves stay package-served by design (#1151/gh-1164): the system prompt advertises `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and the `read` tool serves the embedded copy with zero filesystem access (core, host-independent — regression-pinned by `test/skills/builtin_skills_test.dart`). No re-seeding to disk: that would resurrect the exact drift/shadowing the retirement killed (on-disk copies shadow builtins in discovery precedence).

## Delivered vs remaining

- Delivered: ghost empty skill dirs pruned (incl. already-ghosted devices, next launch); user files/overrides untouched; regression test `upgrade path prunes skill directories the cleanup empties` covering prune-on-remove, repair-already-empty (the filed device state), user-file survival, plus an end-to-end `read builtin://skills/js-apps/SKILL.md` through the real read tool on the mobile-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`.
- Remaining (by design, not this bug): builtins are intentionally not materialized to `.fah/skills/<name>/` on disk; agents should follow the prompt's `builtin://` locations. The iOS WASI shell `ls`/`cat` visibility split is #1335 (separate seam — the `read` tool path is env-free and unaffected).

## Verification (honest disclosure)

- System dart/flutter on this box is machine-guarded (EPERM/137, known); verified via temp Flutter SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, Dart 3.x) + fleet pub cache + `BOT=false` + CI-style placeholder `.env`.
- RED→GREEN: the new test reproduced the exact filed state first (`.fah/skills` = `['create-goal','fa-self-config','js-apps']` empty dirs), then passed after the fix.
- `flutter test test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart` → 15/15 (all pre-existing #1151/gh-1164 pins hold); `dart analyze` on the two changed files → clean (one pre-existing `unused_import` warning on pristine main, untouched); `dart format` clean.
- Not verified on a real device (no simulator here): acceptance is CI + post-merge. Exact device repro for QA: install ≤1.0.510 → seed skills → upgrade to a build with this fix → launch once → Files view / agent `ls .fah/skills/` shows no empty `js-apps/`, `create-goal/`, `fa-self-config/` dirs; agent `read` of each prompt-advertised `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` returns the body.

Fixes #1334

# pr-1342: fix(1334): prune skill directories the seed retirement leaves empty

## Description

## Root cause

Not a sync/materialization bug — the dirs are **deliberate leftovers of the skills retirement** (gh-1164 / #1151, shipped in v1.0.511+): on launch the app removes app-seeded `SKILL.md` copies that byte-match the retired fingerprints (`create-goal`, `fa-self-config`, js-apps per-platform variants) **but leaves their directories behind**. A device upgraded from a pre-#1151 build ends up with exactly three empty dirs under `.fah/skills/` — the filed symptom. They are invisible to discovery (builtins still serve from the package), but glaringly visible to an exploring agent: `ls .fah/skills/` shows skill names with no bodies, reading as "directories created, file writes skipped". Combined with agent memory still referencing the old `.fah/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` paths, the session concluded skills were broken. `.fah/widget-sources/` is unrelated: it is materialized on demand by the `apps_catalog` tool.

## Fix

`_seedBundledSkills` (flutter_app) collapses its two duplicate retire loops into one `_retireSeededCopy` helper that, after removing a retired `SKILL.md`, **also removes the skill directory when it is left empty**:

- dir with a surviving user file (script/notes dropped next to a seed) stays — the review -HUjo guarantee holds;
- a customized copy (byte-mismatch = user override) is never touched;
- the empty-dir prune also fires when the copy is **already gone**, so devices already on 1.0.519/520 — the filed field state — repair on their next launch without a reinstall;
- missing dirs are a no-op (fresh installs never see ghost dirs).

Skill bodies themselves stay package-served by design (#1151/gh-1164): the system prompt advertises `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and the `read` tool serves the embedded copy with zero filesystem access (core, host-independent — regression-pinned by `test/skills/builtin_skills_test.dart`). No re-seeding to disk: that would resurrect the exact drift/shadowing the retirement killed (on-disk copies shadow builtins in discovery precedence).

## Delivered vs remaining

- Delivered: ghost empty skill dirs pruned (incl. already-ghosted devices, next launch); user files/overrides untouched; regression test `upgrade path prunes skill directories the cleanup empties` covering prune-on-remove, repair-already-empty (the filed device state), user-file survival, plus an end-to-end `read builtin://skills/js-apps/SKILL.md` through the real read tool on the mobile-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`.
- Remaining (by design, not this bug): builtins are intentionally not materialized to `.fah/skills/<name>/` on disk; agents should follow the prompt's `builtin://` locations. The iOS WASI shell `ls`/`cat` visibility split is #1335 (separate seam — the `read` tool path is env-free and unaffected).

## Verification (honest disclosure)

- System dart/flutter on this box is machine-guarded (EPERM/137, known); verified via temp Flutter SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, Dart 3.x) + fleet pub cache + `BOT=false` + CI-style placeholder `.env`.
- RED→GREEN: the new test reproduced the exact filed state first (`.fah/skills` = `['create-goal','fa-self-config','js-apps']` empty dirs), then passed after the fix.
- `flutter test test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart` → 15/15 (all pre-existing #1151/gh-1164 pins hold); `dart analyze` on the two changed files → clean (one pre-existing `unused_import` warning on pristine main, untouched); `dart format` clean.
- Not verified on a real device (no simulator here): acceptance is CI + post-merge. Exact device repro for QA: install ≤1.0.510 → seed skills → upgrade to a build with this fix → launch once → Files view / agent `ls .fah/skills/` shows no empty `js-apps/`, `create-goal/`, `fa-self-config/` dirs; agent `read` of each prompt-advertised `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` returns the body.

Fixes #1334

    "summary": "fix(1334): prune skill directories the seed retirement leaves empty",
    "description": "## Root cause

Not a sync/materialization bug — the dirs are **deliberate leftovers of the skills retirement** (gh-1164 / #1151, shipped in v1.0.511+): on launch the app removes app-seeded `SKILL.md` copies that byte-match the retired fingerprints (`create-goal`, `fa-self-config`, js-apps per-platform variants) **but leaves their directories behind**. A device upgraded from a pre-#1151 build ends up with exactly three empty dirs under `.fah/skills/` — the filed symptom. They are invisible to discovery (builtins still serve from the package), but glaringly visible to an exploring agent: `ls .fah/skills/` shows skill names with no bodies, reading as "directories created, file writes skipped". Combined with agent memory still referencing the old `.fah/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` paths, the session concluded skills were broken. `.fah/widget-sources/` is unrelated: it is materialized on demand by the `apps_catalog` tool.

## Fix

`_seedBundledSkills` (flutter_app) collapses its two duplicate retire loops into one `_retireSeededCopy` helper that, after removing a retired `SKILL.md`, **also removes the skill directory when it is left empty**:

- dir with a surviving user file (script/notes dropped next to a seed) stays — the review -HUjo guarantee holds;
- a customized copy (byte-mismatch = user override) is never touched;
- the empty-dir prune also fires when the copy is **already gone**, so devices already on 1.0.519/520 — the filed field state — repair on their next launch without a reinstall;
- missing dirs are a no-op (fresh installs never see ghost dirs).

Skill bodies themselves stay package-served by design (#1151/gh-1164): the system prompt advertises `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and the `read` tool serves the embedded copy with zero filesystem access (core, host-independent — regression-pinned by `test/skills/builtin_skills_test.dart`). No re-seeding to disk: that would resurrect the exact drift/shadowing the retirement killed (on-disk copies shadow builtins in discovery precedence).

## Delivered vs remaining

- Delivered: ghost empty skill dirs pruned (incl. already-ghosted devices, next launch); user files/overrides untouched; regression test `upgrade path prunes skill directories the cleanup empties` covering prune-on-remove, repair-already-empty (the filed device state), user-file survival, plus an end-to-end `read builtin://skills/js-apps/SKILL.md` through the real read tool on the mobile-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`.
- Remaining (by design, not this bug): builtins are intentionally not materialized to `.fah/skills/<name>/` on disk; agents should follow the prompt's `builtin://` locations. The iOS WASI shell `ls`/`cat` visibility split is #1335 (separate seam — the `read` tool path is env-free and unaffected).

## Verification (honest disclosure)

- System dart/flutter on this box is machine-guarded (EPERM/137, known); verified via temp Flutter SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, Dart 3.x) + fleet pub cache + `BOT=false` + CI-style placeholder `.env`.

- Not verified on a real device (no simulator here): acceptance is CI + post-merge. Fixes #1334"

{

  "fields": {
    "summary": "fix(1334): prune skill directories the seed retirement leaves empty",
    "description": "## Root cause

Not a sync/materialization bug — the dirs are **deliberate leftovers of the skills retirement** (gh-1164 / #1151, shipped in v1.0.511+): on launch the app removes app-seeded `SKILL.md` copies that byte-match the retired fingerprints (`create-goal`, `fa-self-config`, js-apps per-platform variants) **but leaves their directories behind**. A device upgraded from a pre-#1151 build ends up with exactly three empty dirs under `.fah/skills/` — the filed symptom. They are invisible to discovery (builtins still serve from the package), but glaringly visible to an exploring agent: `ls .fah/skills/` shows skill names with no bodies, reading as "directories created, file writes skipped". Combined with agent memory still referencing the old `.fah/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` paths, the session concluded skills were broken. `.fah/widget-sources/` is unrelated: it is materialized on demand by the `apps_catalog` tool.

## Fix

`_seedBundledSkills` (flutter_app) collapses its two duplicate retire loops into one `_retireSeededCopy` helper that, after removing a retired `SKILL.md`, **also removes the skill directory when it is left empty**:

- dir with a surviving user file (script/notes dropped next to a seed) stays — the review -HUjo guarantee holds;
- a customized copy (byte-mismatch = user override) is never touched;
- the empty-dir prune also fires when the copy is **already gone**, so devices already on 1.0.519/520 — the filed field state — repair on their next launch without a reinstall;
- missing dirs are a no-op (fresh installs never see ghost dirs).

Skill bodies themselves stay package-served by design (#1151/gh-1164): the system prompt advertises `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and the `read` tool serves the embedded copy with zero filesystem access (core, host-independent — regression-pinned by `test/skills/builtin_skills_test.dart`). No re-seeding to disk: that would resurrect the exact drift/shadowing the retirement killed (on-disk copies shadow builtins in discovery precedence).

## Delivered vs remaining

- Delivered: ghost empty skill dirs pruned (incl. already-ghosted devices, next launch); user files/overrides untouched; regression test `upgrade path prunes skill directories the cleanup empties` covering prune-on-remove, repair-already-empty (the filed device state), user-file survival, plus an end-to-end `read builtin://skills/js-apps/SKILL.md` through the real read tool on the mobile-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`.
- Remaining (by design, not this bug): builtins are intentionally not materialized to `.fah/skills/<name>/` on disk; agents should follow the prompt's `builtin://` locations. The iOS WASI shell `ls`/`cat` visibility split is #1335 (separate seam — the `read` tool path is env-free and unaffected).

## Verification (honest disclosure)

- System dart/flutter on this box is machine-guarded (EPERM/137, known); verified via temp Flutter SDK (`flutter-sdk-1156`, Dart 3.x) + fleet pub cache + `BOT=false` + CI-style placeholder `.env`.
- RED→GREEN: the new test reproduced the exact filed state first (`.fah/skills` = `['create-goal','fa-self-config','js-apps']` empty dirs), then passed after the fix.
- `flutter test test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart` → 15/15 (all pre-existing #1151/gh-1164 pins hold); `dart analyze` on the two changed files → clean (one pre-existing `unused_import` warning on pristine main, untouched); `dart format` clean.
- Not verified on a real device (no simulator here): acceptance is CI + post-merge. Exact device repro for QA: install ≤1.0.510 → seed skills → upgrade to a build with this fix → launch once → Files view / agent `ls .fah/skills/` shows no empty `js-apps/`, `create-goal/`, `fa-self-config/` dirs; agent `read` of each prompt-advertised `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` returns the body.

Fixes #1334"

The app-crap-gate check earlier showed: "Flutter app CRAP ratchet | completed | cancelled | 112478318697". So the "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" job got cancelled mid-run (likely by the concurrency group when a new push arrived — the branch got a merge at 20:20 while the CRAP job was still running; cancellation via `concurrency`).

So the red was NOT a test failure or code issue — it was a cancelled job. On re-run (the 20:18 attempt), the CRAP job stayed cancelled (a re-run of failed jobs doesn't re-run cancelled ones, or it was cancelled again by the newer push at 20:20).

blocks.text:
All three "PR #1342" runs were CodeQL Analyze runs, not the main CI workflow. So the only full CI validations were:
1. push-event CI run 37523344821 on 2598bccd92 (branch) → all 30 listed jobs success, run marked cancelled, and later a re-run attempt had the Quality gate fail on `app-crap-gate = cancelled`.
2. No CI on the newer heads (7ae295cb65, 1c628d4617) yet — push CI didn't trigger for those (possibly because merges by the bot don't trigger, or the workflow's push trigger has filters).

Interesting: check runs for 2598bccd92 include "PR #1342"-style pull_request checks? The check list showed fa_ui tests, Binaries (PR), etc. — those belonged to run 37523344821 (push CI), whose jobs are named like "Flutter app tests (shard 0/2)" etc. Hmm wait, the check runs for 2598bccd92 earlier showed names like "fa_ui tests (shard 1/3)", "Binaries (PR) (ubuntu-24.04-arm...)" — but jobs of run 37523344821 showed "PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ...)", "Core tests (shard ...)", "Flutter app tests (shard ...)". So the check-runs list mixed multiple runs' checks on the same sha (e.g., the "PR #1342" CodeQL + push CI + office add-in).

The critical failure: "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" job 112478318697 → cancelled. Created AFTER the run 37523344821 attempt-1 jobs (112474xxxx)? 112478318697 > 112474768633. Yes, so it was created later — hmm, this suggests the CRAP job was part of a re-run attempt or was a `workflow_run`-triggered job ("Flutter app CRAP ratchet" — separate workflow triggered by workflow_run, gated on CI). And there's also "CRAP + duplication | completed | success | 112477856650" and "Coverage ratchet | success" in the 2598bccd92 check list — those are workflow_run-triggered followers.

So "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" (id 112478318697, cancelled) is its own workflow that runs AFTER CI. It got cancelled. Then "Quality gate" — wait, the Quality gate job is part of CI workflow (run 37523344821). The re-run at 20:17:46-20:18:35 (attempt 2, only re-running failed/cancelled jobs? Actually re-run "failed jobs" re-runs failed AND cancelled jobs...). The Quality gate attempt-2 read R_CRAP=cancelled (the CRAP ratchet follower stayed cancelled) and correctly failed.

Hmm OK wait, actually the Quality gate job of the CI run reads `R_CRAP` env from... it printed "app-crap-gate = cancelled". The CRAP ratchet job 112478318697 was cancelled at some point before 20:17:46.

Why was the CRAP ratchet cancelled? Possibly concurrency (workflow_run follower with concurrency group cancel-in-progress: newer run started when main CI at 20:21 ran?) or the merge bot cancelled it. Honestly, the precise infra reason doesn't change the rework plan.

**Now: what does the rework need to do?**

Per the discussion thread:
- "Validation CI went red on the head ... it fixes the findings and pushes; your own push re-runs validation just the same."
- "🔴 red head 2598bccd9 — red 1/3 ... after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head"
- "🔁 guest rework arm 1/2"

So the rework agent (me) should: investigate the red, fix anything actually broken, push a new head (which resets the red counter), and reply to the thread.

Is anything actually broken in the code? Evidence so far:
- All attempt-1 CI legs on 2598bccd92 passed (30/30 success): static, core tests, flutter analyze, flutter tests (incl. the new test), faui, builds, PTY, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer, pin-gate...
- CRAP + duplication: success. Coverage ratchet: success.
- The only cancelled: "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" (a follower workflow) — cancelled, never got to evaluate.
- Then Quality gate (attempt 2) failed BECAUSE the CRAP ratchet was cancelled (it requires success-or-skipped).

So the red is NOT a code defect — it's a cancelled-by-infra leg. But I can't just claim that: as the rework agent I should verify the PR is actually sound on the current head:
1. Verify the two changed files against the current main-merged head (1c628d4617) — the merges from main touched ci.yml, cli files, dart_tui vendor. Did anything in those merges conflict with or invalidate the PR's changes? The PR touches flutter_app files only; the merges touched .github/workflows/ci.yml, lib/src/cli/*, vendor/dart_tui. No overlap → still coherent.
2. Run the PR's test suite locally (at least flutter_app skills_toggles_store_test.dart + related) on the current head to confirm GREEN.
3. Check the CRAP ratchet config — will "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" pass once it actually runs on this PR? Let me look at what it does: .github/workflows — find the workflow. It's probably a ratchet on crap4dart metrics for flutter_app. The PR modified flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_skills.dart — collapsing two loops into a helper function. CRAP = complexity² × (1-coverage%) + complexity. If the helper has higher complexity than before and coverage in that area is low, the ratchet (which fails if CRAP increases beyond baseline) could fail! The baseline .crap-baseline.json exists in repo root and there's crap4dart.yaml with thresholds. Let me check what the baseline says for agent_service_skills.dart and whether the new code exceeds it.

That's the key risk: when the CRAP ratchet actually runs on a new head, it might go red for real. Let me inspect.

All `PR #1342` runs were CodeQL; the only full CI validation was the push run whose CRAP-ratchet follower got cancelled, and the aggregate gate then refused a `cancelled` leg. The real risk: once the CRAP ratchet actually runs on a new head, will it pass? Let me inspect the workflow and the baseline.

# Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them
  # into ONE lcov (union DA hits, never cat — same as the core guards)
  # and runs the pinned crap4dart against flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
  # It is also the only home of the config guards: badge sync (AC1),
  # generated-exclude parity (E1) and the only-down git-history threshold
  # guard (AC3) — a raised threshold cannot merge, a new one (bootstrap)
  # can.
  app-crap-gate:
    name: Flutter app CRAP ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, flutter-tests]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no app/shared changes — flutter_app CRAP green-skipped (required context reported)"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # only-down guard diffs thresholds against the base
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - name: Pub cache (crap4dart)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}
          restore-keys: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: app-coverage-shard-*
          path: app-coverage-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          count=$(ls app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "2" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 2 app shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p flutter_app/coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info \
            app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: Config guards — badge sync, exclude parity, only-down (AC1/E1/AC3)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          [ -n "$BASE_SHA" ] || BASE_SHA=HEAD~1
          python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 (analyzer 14.4 refresh).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 <0.12.0 — same bounded pin as the core job;
          # 0.11.0 carries the Type-2 duplication gate the repo pins to.
          # coverage.run_tests: false in both configs — the merged shard
          # lcov above is the source; never re-run the suite here.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json > crap_report.json

      # Issue #490 AC2: publish the ranked CRAP JSON even when the ratchet
      # is red (analyze writes the report to stdout before its non-zero
      # exit) — descents rank from this artifact, never from a local
      # ad-hoc run.
      - name: Upload crap_report.json artifact (issue 490 AC2)
        if: always() && (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: crap_report
          path: flutter_app/crap_report.json
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Pixel and flutter gates over test/golden/goldens (issue 447)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart check

  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  # duration-balanced manifest (scripts/faui_test_shards.json, rebalanced
  # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml), one file executed by exactly ONE shard,
  # goldens excluded exactly as before (host-locked). Shards fan out INSIDE
  # the job graph; only the aggregate Quality gate is a required check, so
  # a red shard = red gate and path-skipped = neutral (AC4 semantics). A
  # single failed matrix leg can be rerun alone via "Re-run failed jobs"
  # (E1) — the gate then re-aggregates the same results.
  test-faui:
    name: fa_ui tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 12
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0

# Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them
  # into ONE lcov (union DA hits, never cat — same as the core guards)
  # and runs the pinned crap4dart against flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
  # It is also the only home of the config guards: badge sync (AC1),
  # generated-exclude parity (E1) and the only-down git-history threshold
  # guard (AC3) — a raised threshold cannot merge, a new one (bootstrap)
  # can.
  app-crap-gate:
    name: Flutter app CRAP ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, flutter-tests]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no app/shared changes — flutter_app CRAP green-skipped (required context reported)"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # only-down guard diffs thresholds against the base
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - name: Pub cache (crap4dart)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}
          restore-keys: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: app-coverage-shard-*
          path: app-coverage-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          count=$(ls app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "2" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 2 app shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p flutter_app/coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info \
            app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: Config guards — badge sync, exclude parity, only-down (AC1/E1/AC3)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          [ -n "$BASE_SHA" ] || BASE_SHA=HEAD~1
          python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 (analyzer 14.4 refresh).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 <0.12.0 — same bounded pin as the core job;
          # 0.11.0 carries the Type-2 duplication gate the repo pins to.
          # coverage.run_tests: false in both configs — the merged shard
          # lcov above is the source; never re-run the suite here.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json > crap_report.json

      # Issue #490 AC2: publish the ranked CRAP JSON even when the ratchet
      # is red (analyze writes the report to stdout before its non-zero
      # exit) — descents rank from this artifact, never from a local
      # ad-hoc run.
      - name: Upload crap_report.json artifact (issue 490 AC2)
        if: always() && (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: crap_report
          path: flutter_app/crap_report.json
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Pixel and flutter gates over test/golden/goldens (issue 447)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart check

  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  # duration-balanced manifest (scripts/faui_test_shards.json, rebalanced
  # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml), one file executed by exactly ONE shard,
  # goldens excluded exactly as before (host-locked). Shards fan out INSIDE
  # the job graph; only the aggregate Quality gate is a required check, so
  # a red shard = red gate and path-skipped = neutral (AC4 semantics). A
  # single failed matrix leg can be rerun alone via "Re-run failed jobs"
  # (E1) — the gate then re-aggregates the same results.
  test-faui:

          channel: stable

# crap4dart configuration for the flutter_app package.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET (issue #433): the threshold is pinned at the CURRENT worst score
# measured by the SAME pipeline the CI gate uses — `flutter test --coverage`
# lcov (E2: widget-test coverage differs from the core's dart lcov, so the
# number must come from this pipeline, not the core's).
# Bootstrap (2026-09-15): 2450.0 — `JsAppEngine._faCall` (CC 49, 0% line
# coverage). Descent #1 (same day): the issue's three named offenders went
# under the next milestone line (CRAP ≤ 40 each) and the threshold followed
# the measured new worst: 2450.0 → 870.0 (`wasm_shell_git.run` and
# `main`, CC 29 at 0% coverage). Descent #2 (issue #475): both beasts
# decomposed into route-table dispatch + per-family handlers with a 51-test
# golden suite, and the cluster's own 812/702/600/506 beasts went down with
# them; the threshold follows the new measured worst: 870.0 → 650.0
# (`runCodemieSsoFlow`, CC 25 at 0% cov — another lane's ladder card).
# Descent #9 (issue #485): the on-device provider stream functions moved to
# one shared pump + codec walk (lib/on_device/), and the beasts went down
# with them — gemma 992 → 9, transformers.js 552/506 → 17/1, webllm 420 → 6
# (all fully covered by the provider suites + the new codec-table/pump
# tests); the threshold follows the measured new worst: 650.0 → 380.0
# (`WasiSandboxShell._runStage`, CC 19 at 0% cov — the wasm_shell cluster,
# another lane's ladder card).
# Pushes may only make the codebase BETTER,
# never worse; scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down rejects a raised
# threshold in CI. The staged ladder continues in follow-up cards:
# 870 → … → 40 (see AGENTS.md "Quality gates"). Re-measure after each fix:
# cd flutter_app && flutter test --coverage &&
# dart pub global run crap4dart analyze.

sources: [lib]

# Same generated set as the root config (E1 parity — asserted by
# scripts/check_crap_guards.py).
exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in flutter_app/lib under the flutter lcov
  # pipeline. Descent #10 (issue #558): the wasm_shell pipeline-engine
  # cluster went down (_runStage 380→4, _runPipeline 210→4, _evalExpr
  # 182→3, _rewriteRelativeArgs 110→2, _maybeRewritePath 72→3, all 100%
  # covered by test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart); the threshold follows
  # the measured new worst: 380.0 → 272.0 (`WasiSandboxShell._xargsBuiltin`,
  # CC 16 at 0% cov — the wasm_shell builtins cluster, the next lane's
  # ladder card). Only down.
  # Descent #11 (issue #559): the wasm_shell builtins cluster went down
  # (xargs 272→7, _parsePrimary 210→3, _testBuiltin 132→9, du 132→3,
  # tac 90→6, tr 25.9→4, pip 72→3, _expandTrSet 30.8→gone — table/spec
  # driven parse helpers now live in wasm_shell_builtins.dart with direct
  # unit tests, the exec halves are covered e2e in
  # test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart); the threshold follows the
  # measured new worst: 272.0 → 210.0 (`GemmaService.chatStream`, CC 14
  # at 0% cov — another lane's ladder card). Only down.
  # Descent #12 (issue #701): the 0%-coverage trio went down (_statBuiltin
  # 156→12.1 @ 91% cov via test/wasm_shell_stat_test.dart, isFaCliInstalled
  # 110→6 via the extracted faCliProbe seam + test/sessions_root_test.dart,
  # _showAppMenu 90→9 @ 100% cov via test/apps/apps_panel_menu_test.dart);
  # the threshold follows the measured new worst: 210.0 → 30.0 (the CC-5
  # 0%-cov tier: routeExtHostMessage, codemie _createController, attached
  # _AttachedRow.build, GemmaService.loadModel — the next ladder cards).
  # Re-measured on the CI pipeline (app-crap-gate run 35479048998): local
  # lcov is impossible on the agent cube (the flutter coverage collector
  # canonicalizes source paths and lstat EPERMs through .worktrees). Only
  # down.
  # TEMP raise (owner call 2026-09-26, mirrors dmtools-dart #256): the #955
  # network-mode merge shipped widgets without tests — max CRAP 72.0
  # (_ChannelRailState._createChannel, CC 8 @ 0% cov). Restore to 30.0 via
  # the linked issue.
  # raise-issue: gh-992
  # Restored (gh-992, 2026-09-27): the agents/enroll DAP-tab rework
  # (fcd2d0232) covered the #955 network UI — 5 enroll dialog groups +
  # channel_rail/chat_page call-site suites, 72 focused tests; re-measured
  # on the full local flutter lcov (3292 green): max CRAP 30.0, the
  # threshold follows back down 75.0 → 30.0. Only down.
  threshold: 30.0

coverage:
  # The CI app-crap-gate job merges the two flutter-tests shard reports
  # (scripts/merge_lcov.py) right before the CRAP step. Pre-commit stays
  # core-only: flutter coverage is too heavy for every commit.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  # flutter's lcov carries no BRDA branch records; branch coverage stays
  # a core-package gate concern.
  branch_coverage: false
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole flutter suite
  # first. Coverage comes from the CI shard merge (scripts/merge_lcov.py)
  # and pre-commit stays core-only (#433 split); nobody wants a second
  # suite run inside a 6-minute gate job.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This config is the single source of which gates `crap4dart check` runs
# (CI app-crap-gate job, pre-commit core hook): 0.9.5 default-enables ALL
# built-in gates, so everything not enforced below is disabled explicitly.
gates:
  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet below already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  duplication: {enabled: false} # own jscpd <1% guard (global %) — 0.10.0's
    # `duplication.sources` cross-module key stays available if the jscpd
    # guards are ever retired (mirrors the root crap4dart.yaml)
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over the golden set (165 PNGs). severity: warning + the
  # excludes below are the documented INTERIM mitigation (#447): the
  # 0.9.5 detector knows only 3 shapes — it missed both classes that
  # broke the 40 pre-font goldens of de2f11b9 (solid Ahem text
  # rectangles, hollow icon squares without an X) and false-positives on:
  #   - the Habit Tracker checkmark tile (green square + white V
  #     converging like an X signature; light theme only, the same 22px
  #     tile at x=234 in all 5 hits),
  #   - the yellow "25:00" digits on the dark timer card (row y=195 of
  #     apps_panel/panel_dark: yellow glyph edges alternate with the
  #     dark card ≥8px with ≥4 transitions — passes the stripe
  #     heuristic).
  # Each exclude is an upstream IstiN/crap4dart bug. Flip to
  # `severity: error` and drop the excludes when the upstream detector
  # fixes land — scripts/check_golden_detector.py re-verifies all six
  # classes against this exact detector (see its docstring).
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test/golden/goldens]
    exclude:
      # false positives: green checkmark tile reads as an X (light theme)
      - 'test/golden/goldens/launcher/grid_light.png'
      - 'test/golden/goldens/launcher/sheet_bar_light.png'
      - 'test/golden/goldens/launcher/sheet_bar_streaming_light.png'
      - 'test/golden/goldens/launcher/grid_widget_tile_light.png'
      - 'test/golden/goldens/onboarding_p4_light_phone.png'
      # false positive: yellow "25:00" digits read as overflow stripes (dark)
      - 'test/golden/goldens/apps_panel/panel_dark.png'

  # Widget → golden coverage. WARNING (not error): the 0.9.5 widget
  # census is broader than the enforced test/golden/golden_guard_test.dart
  # list — 10.5% of lib/ widgets have goldens today. Flip to error when
  # the census reaches parity with the guard (follow-up card).
  golden:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning

  # Tooltips/labels — the app ships to stores. WARNING: 28+ interactive
  # widgets lack labels today (InkWell/GestureDetector semantics).
  # Flip to error after the a11y sweep card lands.
  accessibility:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning

  # l10n discipline (we already ship _ru goldens). WARNING: the sweep of
  # remaining labelText/hintText/tooltip literals is pending.
  # Flip to error when lib/ is clean.
  hardcoded_strings:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning

blocks.text:
# Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them
  # into ONE lcov (union DA hits, never cat — same as the core guards)
  # and runs the pinned crap4dart against flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
  # It is also the only home of the config guards: badge sync (AC1),
  # generated-exclude parity (E1) and the only-down git-history threshold
  # guard (AC3) — a raised threshold cannot merge, a new one (bootstrap)
  # can.
  app-crap-gate:
    name: Flutter app CRAP ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, flutter-tests]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no app/shared changes — flutter_app CRAP green-skipped (required context reported)"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # only-down guard diffs thresholds against the base
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - name: Pub cache (crap4dart)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}
          restore-keys: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: app-coverage-shard-*
          path: app-coverage-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          count=$(ls app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "2" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 2 app shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p flutter_app/coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info \
            app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: Config guards — badge sync, exclude parity, only-down (AC1/E1/AC3)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          [ -n "$BASE_SHA" ] || BASE_SHA=HEAD~1
          python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 (analyzer 14.4 refresh).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 <0.12.0 — same bounded pin as the core job;
          # 0.11.0 carries the Type-2 duplication gate the repo pins to.
          # coverage.run_tests: false in both configs — the merged shard
          # lcov above is the source; never re-run the suite here.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json > crap_report.json

      # Issue #490 AC2: publish the ranked CRAP JSON even when the ratchet
      # is red (analyze writes the report to stdout before its non-zero
      # exit) — descents rank from this artifact, never from a local
      # ad-hoc run.
      - name: Upload crap_report.json artifact (issue 490 AC2)
        if: always() && (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: crap_report
          path: flutter_app/crap_report.json
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Pixel and flutter gates over test/golden/goldens (issue 447)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart check

  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  # duration-balanced manifest (scripts/faui_test_shards.json, rebalanced
  # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml), one file executed by exactly ONE shard,
  # goldens excluded exactly as before (host-locked). Shards fan out INSIDE
  # the job graph; only the aggregate Quality gate is a required check, so
  # a red shard = red gate and path-skipped = neutral (AC4 semantics). A
  # single failed matrix leg can be rerun alone via "Re-run failed jobs"
  # (E1) — the gate then re-aggregates the same results.
  test-faui:
    name: fa_ui tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 12
    permissions:

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

        with:
          channel: stable

  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them

  # and runs the pinned crap4dart against flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.

  # generated-exclude parity (E1) and the only-down git-history threshold

  app-crap-gate:
    name: Flutter app CRAP ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, flutter-tests]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:

    steps:

content.text:
# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.

blocks.text:
Now I know why validation CI was red:

**"Quality gate FAILED: a leg is cancelled (app-crap-gate)"** — the `app-crap-gate` leg was **cancelled** (not failed, not skipped). Everything else was success/skipped.

The app-crap-gate check earlier showed: "Flutter app CRAP ratchet | completed | cancelled | 112478318697". So the "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" job got cancelled mid-run (likely by the concurrency group when a new push arrived — the branch got a merge at 20:20 while the CRAP job was still running; cancellation via `concurrency`).

So the red was NOT a test failure or code issue — it was a cancelled job. On re-run (the 20:18 attempt), the CRAP job stayed cancelled (a re-run of failed jobs doesn't re-run cancelled ones, or it was cancelled again by the newer push at 20:20).

Now the important question: what should the rework do?

1. The current head (1c628d4617) is a fresh head. Per owner directive: "after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head". The head has moved (1c628d4617). My job as the armed rework agent: make sure the PR is in good shape, push if needed (new head resets the red counter), and reply to the thread.

2. But wait — is there anything actually wrong with the code? The CRAP gate cancellation was mechanical (cancelled by concurrency), not a code defect. However, I should verify the PR's own tests still pass on the current head (which includes merges from main). The PR description says "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" got cancelled — that's the flutter_app CRAP ratchet job. There's a `.crap-baseline.json` in repo root. A CRAP ratchet might fail if the new test code increases complexity... but it was cancelled, not failed.

Key consideration: could the new test itself trip the CRAP ratchet once it actually runs? The test added ~50 lines to `flutter_app/test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart`. CRAP (Change Risk Anti-Patterns) measures cyclomatic complexity × coverage. Test files usually aren't counted in CRAP baselines (only lib code).
