# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.

KEY finding: 

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]     # push CI only on main!
  workflow_dispatch: ... # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads: pushes fire NO CI —
  # the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
  # this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules)
```

So: pushes to the PR branch fire NO CI. Validation on PR heads is dispatched by the SM (state machine) when "validation is due (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules)". The earlier CI run 37523344821 on the branch at 20:01:52 was such a dispatch (triggered by the SM). It went red on app-crap-gate=cancelled.

Wait — the run's event: let me verify run 37523344821's event was workflow_dispatch. Also the red was on the OLD head 2598bccd9; the head has since moved (merges at 20:20 and 20:27 — from the merge bot "sm-silent-update"). Since pushes fire no CI, validation on the NEW head 1c628d4617 will be dispatched by the SM when due.

Now — "after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head" — red 1/3 on 2598bccd9. The SM's rules: the rework agent is armed (arm 1/2 used?). "🔁 guest rework arm 1/2" means arm 1 of 2 was consumed? This session is presumably arm... hmm, "guest rework arm 1/2" might mean this arming is 1 of max 2.

So what does the SM expect from me (the rework agent)?
1. Investigate the red → done: app-crap-gate leg was cancelled, not failed. No code defect.
2. Fix findings and push → the finding is "validation went red". Since the cause was a cancelled leg (infra), the "fix" is to let validation re-run. A new head already exists (1c628d4617). The SM will dispatch validation on it when due. Do I need to push anything? If the rework pushes (even an empty chore commit), the head changes and validation re-runs fresh. But the guidance also says don't add unrequested commits... The rework contract: "it fixes the findings and pushes; your own push re-runs validation just the same."

Given:
- The PR content is unchanged since my session started; working tree clean at 1c628d4617.
- Validation hasn't run on 1c628d4617 at all yet (dispatch-only).

Hmm, but will the SM dispatch validation on 1c628d4617 automatically? "the SM ... dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules)". A new head (from the merge bot) should make validation due again. The red head was 2598bccd9; the merge bot pushed new heads at 20:20 and 20:27. The SM's red-slot logic: "after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head" — red is 1/3, so validation isn't blocked.

But hold on — why is the rework agent (me) even triggered then? Because when validation went red, the SM armed the rework agent to fix the red. The arm comment says the rework agent fixes findings and pushes. The findings here: none in code — the red was a cancelled leg. The honest rework output: 
- Investigate the red, document the root cause (cancelled app-crap-gate leg; no code defect).
- Verify locally that the PR is green (run the tests: flutter analyze, the changed test file, skills toggles suite, and ideally the CRAP-sensitive surface).
- Push a new head so validation re-runs on a fresh SHA (this also serves as the "fixes the findings and pushes" behavior — the new head re-runs validation).

Wait, should I really push? Let me think about the alternatives:
a) Push nothing; just reply to the thread explaining the red was a cancelled leg and validation will re-dispatch on the current head. Risk: the SM may be waiting specifically for the rework agent's push to re-arm validation ("your own push re-runs validation just the same"). If I don't push and the SM doesn't re-dispatch (because from its view the head is "dirty" — a merge happened), validation could stall. Hmm.

Actually, look at the timeline: head 1c628d4617 was pushed at 20:27:32 by the merge bot (sm-silent-update). If the SM planned to dispatch validation on it, it would have done so or will shortly. The rework run (me) started at 20:30:34 — armed by the red. The directive says "the rework agent is armed on this PR — it fixes the findings and pushes; your own push re-runs validation just the same."

Given the machine loop design, the SAFEST and most contract-conformant action: verify everything locally, then push a new head (e.g., the merge-updated branch is already new — but pushing MY commit creates an even newer head ensuring validation re-dispatch). But what commit? I have no code findings... 

Hmm, wait. Let me re-check whether there are REAL findings I'm missing. The ai-teammate comment is generic ("Validation CI went red"). The actual red: app-crap-gate cancelled. Is there any chance the app-crap-gate would FAIL (not cancel) on this PR's code? If yes, pushing without fixing would just go red again (2/3!). That's the real risk to check: the CRAP ratchet on the PR's refactored code with the merged shard coverage.

The PR refactored `_seedBundledSkills` into `_retireSeededCopy` + loops. Let me:
1. Read the current code on the head.
2. Estimate its CC and coverage. CC of `_retireSeededCopy`: branches: try(1) + if body!=null(1) + if !isStale(1) + if leftovers.isOk(1) + && (1) + if empty(1)... roughly CC 6-7. CRAP at coverage c: CC²(1-c) + CC. At c=0 → 49 > 30 threshold! If the new helper is NOT covered by the shard coverage, it'd blow the 30.0 ratchet. But the new test covers it (the test runs in flutter-tests shards and exercises AgentService.create → _seedBundledSkills → _retireSeededCopy with multiple cases). So coverage of this function should be ~100%. But wait — which shard runs skills_toggles_store_test.dart? Both shards run different halves of the test suite; the coverage MERGES both shards (union). So any function covered by ANY test in either shard counts. The CRAP ratchet uses the union — good.

But careful: is `_seedBundledSkills` even executed in widget tests? Yes — the pre-existing tests in skills_toggles_store_test.dart (like 'a fresh env resolves the builtins without any seeded copy') create AgentService with MemoryExecutionEnv, which triggers the seeding path. So `_retireSeededCopy` gets executed. 

However — CRAP counts per-FUNCTION coverage from lcov. The lcov lines for the helper get hit by the new test → cov high → CRAP low. Fine.

But there's a subtlety: `dart pub global run crap4dart analyze` uses lcov + the analyzer's cyclomatic complexity. The old code: `_seedBundledSkills` had 2 loops × (try + if null + if !stale) — CC ~ 11-12? CRAP at 0% could be 132+. But it was covered enough before (threshold 30 held on main with the OLD code — main's head passed the full CI at 20:21, success, including app-crap-gate? main run 37525825919 at 20:21:31 success — that's the push CI on main 34446022c — it would include app-crap-gate since main classifies everything as affected. It succeeded). The PR's refactor REDUCES _seedBundledSkills complexity and adds a small well-covered helper → CRAP strictly improves or stays equal. So the ratchet will pass.

Let me now verify things locally:
1. `dart analyze` / `flutter analyze` on the two changed files (and ideally the flutter_app).
2. Run `flutter test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart` in flutter_app.
3. Possibly run crap4dart analyze with a locally generated lcov — heavy; but there might be a temp flutter SDK from the previous session (flutter-sdk-1156). Let me check.

Also — check AGENTS.md for conventions (it's 124KB; read the relevant sections: maybe a section about rework/validation). Let me search AGENTS.md for "rework" / "red" / "validation" to understand the machine loop expectations.

blocks.text:
===
# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): awf main is load-bearing and review-gated, so
    # pack fixes go live on merge with no re-pin ceremony (recently
    # shipped on main: #579 conflict-rework, #577/#578
    # mutexExcludeSelf-by-fact-of-holding, #576 review-machine-unlinked,
    # #573-#574 pack snapshots + registry env, #572 review-stale-verdict,
    # #571 dmtools self-heal, #570 SM budget 1→3, #569 rework fatality,
    # #568 mergeBot workspace/repository args, #566 pack-registry runner
    # overrides). Accepted trade-off: a mutable ref executes whatever
    # sits at the awf main head at run start. The ENGINE (dmtools-agents)
    # resolves from releases via vars — no factory_ref here. Flip in
    # lockstep with the other machine-loop stubs — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

Now I know why validation CI was red:

**"Quality gate FAILED: a leg is cancelled (app-crap-gate)"** — the `app-crap-gate` leg was **cancelled** (not failed, not skipped). Everything else was success/skipped.

The app-crap-gate check earlier showed: "Flutter app CRAP ratchet | completed | cancelled | 112478318697". So the "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" job got cancelled mid-run (likely by the concurrency group when a new push arrived — the branch got a merge at 20:20 while the CRAP job was still running; cancellation via `concurrency`).

So the red was NOT a test failure or code issue — it was a cancelled job. On re-run (the 20:18 attempt), the CRAP job stayed cancelled (a re-run of failed jobs doesn't re-run cancelled ones, or it was cancelled again by the newer push at 20:20).

Now the important question: what should the rework do?

1. The current head (1c628d4617) is a fresh head. Per owner directive: "after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head". The head has moved (1c628d4617). My job as the armed rework agent: make sure the PR is in good shape, push if needed (new head resets the red counter), and reply to the thread.

2. But wait — is there anything actually wrong with the code? The CRAP gate cancellation was mechanical (cancelled by concurrency), not a code defect. However, I should verify the PR's own tests still pass on the current head (which includes merges from main). The PR description says "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" got cancelled — that's the flutter_app CRAP ratchet job. There's a `.crap-baseline.json` in repo root. A CRAP ratchet might fail if the new test code increases complexity... but it was cancelled, not failed.

Key consideration: could the new test itself trip the CRAP ratchet once it actually runs? The test added ~50 lines to `flutter_app/test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart`. CRAP (Change Risk Anti-Patterns) measures cyclomatic complexity × coverage. Test files usually aren't counted in CRAP baselines (only lib code). The changed lib file is `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_skills.dart`. The refactor collapsed two loops into a helper — that may CHANGE the complexity metrics of the lib file! If the CRAP ratchet has per-function thresholds, the new `_retireSeededCopy` function might exceed a threshold. Let me look at the crap4dart.yaml and .crap-baseline.json to see.

Actually, let me first check the current validation state. The "PR #1342" run on 7ae295cb65 (20:20:14) SUCCEEDED — meaning Quality gate passed there (all legs success or skipped). And that head included the PR's changes! So the PR code passed full validation on 7ae295cb65. Then main moved again (34446022c merged dart_tui fix), and the branch merged main again → 1c628d4617 at 20:27. No CI run on 1c628d4617 yet (no push-triggered CI on the branch? The kicker push run 37526600233 at 20:27:36 succeeded — hmm, that's the kicker workflow, not CI. Wait, was there a CI push run on 1c628d4617? I don't see one in the runs list for the branch... interesting. Actually looking at the runs list for the branch: 1c628d4617 has Machine Merge Bot (cancelled), Office add-in (success), kicker push (success), rework (in_progress). No CI run!

Hmm, why no CI run on 1c628d4617? Because the merge was pushed by the Machine Merge Bot ("sm-silent-update")? Maybe CI push trigger has a condition ([bot] pushes skip?). But "PR #1342" (pull_request synchronize) should have run on the new head... The pull_request run appears as "PR #1342 | refs/pull/1342/head". For 1c628d4617 I don't see a "PR #1342" run. Odd. Maybe it's queued/later, or the pull_request CI for this PR only triggers on classify...

Actually, wait: the pull_request run at 20:20:14 was on 7ae295cb65 which was PR head 20:20-20:27. Hmm, but 1c628d4617 became head at 20:27:32, and my rework session started at 20:30:34. A pull_request synchronize run would have been triggered at 20:27:36ish. Let me check whether there's a queued "PR #1342" run.

Actually, from the first workflow-runs query (page 1, created 19:50-20:35, 100 entries) — I filtered for PR #1342 runs and only saw the rework run + others. Let me search all runs_c/d for "PR #1342" name.

blocks.text:
# Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them
  # into ONE lcov (union DA hits, never cat — same as the core guards)
  # and runs the pinned crap4dart against flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
  # It is also the only home of the config guards: badge sync (AC1),
  # generated-exclude parity (E1) and the only-down git-history threshold
  # guard (AC3) — a raised threshold cannot merge, a new one (bootstrap)
  # can.
  app-crap-gate:
    name: Flutter app CRAP ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, flutter-tests]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no app/shared changes — flutter_app CRAP green-skipped (required context reported)"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # only-down guard diffs thresholds against the base
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - name: Pub cache (crap4dart)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}
          restore-keys: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: app-coverage-shard-*
          path: app-coverage-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          count=$(ls app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "2" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 2 app shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p flutter_app/coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info \
            app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: Config guards — badge sync, exclude parity, only-down (AC1/E1/AC3)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          [ -n "$BASE_SHA" ] || BASE_SHA=HEAD~1
          python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 (analyzer 14.4 refresh).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 <0.12.0 — same bounded pin as the core job;
          # 0.11.0 carries the Type-2 duplication gate the repo pins to.
          # coverage.run_tests: false in both configs — the merged shard
          # lcov above is the source; never re-run the suite here.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json > crap_report.json

      # Issue #490 AC2: publish the ranked CRAP JSON even when the ratchet
      # is red (analyze writes the report to stdout before its non-zero
      # exit) — descents rank from this artifact, never from a local
      # ad-hoc run.
      - name: Upload crap_report.json artifact (issue 490 AC2)
        if: always() && (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: crap_report
          path: flutter_app/crap_report.json
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Pixel and flutter gates over test/golden/goldens (issue 447)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart check

  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  # duration-balanced manifest (scripts/faui_test_shards.json, rebalanced
  # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml), one file executed by exactly ONE shard,
  # goldens excluded exactly as before (host-locked). Shards fan out INSIDE
  # the job graph; only the aggregate Quality gate is a required check, so
  # a red shard = red gate and path-skipped = neutral (AC4 semantics). A
  # single failed matrix leg can be rerun alone via "Re-run failed jobs"
  # (E1) — the gate then re-aggregates the same results.
  test-faui:
    name: fa_ui tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 12
    permissions:

    strategy:

        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.

KEY finding: 

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]     # push CI only on main!
  workflow_dispatch: ... # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads: pushes fire NO CI —
  # the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
  # this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules)
```

So: pushes to the PR branch fire NO CI. Validation on PR heads is dispatched by the SM (state machine) when "validation is due (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules)". The earlier CI run 37523344821 on the branch at 20:01:52 was such a dispatch (triggered by the SM). It went red on app-crap-gate=cancelled.

Wait — the run's event: let me verify run 37523344821's event was workflow_dispatch. Also the red was on the OLD head 2598bccd9; the head has since moved (merges at 20:20 and 20:27 — from the merge bot "sm-silent-update"). Since pushes fire no CI, validation on the NEW head 1c628d4617 will be dispatched by the SM when due.

Now — "after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head" — red 1/3 on 2598bccd9. The SM's rules: the rework agent is armed (arm 1/2 used?). "🔁 guest rework arm 1/2" means arm 1 of 2 was consumed? This session is presumably arm... hmm, "guest rework arm 1/2" might mean this arming is 1 of max 2.

So what does the SM expect from me (the rework agent)?
1. Investigate the red → done: app-crap-gate leg was cancelled, not failed. No code defect.
2. Fix findings and push → the finding is "validation went red". Since the cause was a cancelled leg (infra), the "fix" is to let validation re-run. A new head already exists (1c628d4617). The SM will dispatch validation on it when due. Do I need to push anything? If the rework pushes (even an empty chore commit), the head changes and validation re-runs fresh. But the guidance also says don't add unrequested commits... The rework contract: "it fixes the findings and pushes; your own push re-runs validation just the same."

Given:
- The PR content is unchanged since my session started; working tree clean at 1c628d4617.
- Validation hasn't run on 1c628d4617 at all yet (dispatch-only).

Hmm, but will the SM dispatch validation on 1c628d4617 automatically? "the SM ... dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules)". A new head (from the merge bot) should make validation due again. The red head was 2598bccd9; the merge bot pushed new heads at 20:20 and 20:27. The SM's red-slot logic: "after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head" — red is 1/3, so validation isn't blocked.

But hold on — why is the rework agent (me) even triggered then? Because when validation went red, the SM armed the rework agent to fix the red. The arm comment says the rework agent fixes findings and pushes. The findings here: none in code — the red was a cancelled leg. The honest rework output: 
- Investigate the red, document the root cause (cancelled app-crap-gate leg; no code defect).
- Verify locally that the PR is green (run the tests: flutter analyze, the changed test file, skills toggles suite, and ideally the CRAP-sensitive surface).
- Push a new head so validation re-runs on a fresh SHA (this also serves as the "fixes the findings and pushes" behavior — the new head re-runs validation).

Wait, should I really push? Let me think about the alternatives:
a) Push nothing; just reply to the thread explaining the red was a cancelled leg and validation will re-dispatch on the current head. Risk: the SM may be waiting specifically for the rework agent's push to re-arm validation ("your own push re-runs validation just the same"). If I don't push and the SM doesn't re-dispatch (because from its view the head is "dirty" — a merge happened), validation could stall. Hmm.

Actually, look at the timeline: head 1c628d4617 was pushed at 20:27:32 by the merge bot (sm-silent-update). If the SM planned to dispatch validation on it, it would have done so or will shortly. The rework run (me) started at 20:30:34 — armed by the red. The directive says "the rework agent is armed on this PR — it fixes the findings and pushes; your own push re-runs validation just the same."

Given the machine loop design, the SAFEST and most contract-conformant action: verify everything locally, then push a new head (e.g., the merge-updated branch is already new — but pushing MY commit creates an even newer head ensuring validation re-dispatch). But what commit? I have no code findings... 

Hmm, wait. Let me re-check whether there are REAL findings I'm missing. The ai-teammate comment is generic ("Validation CI went red"). The actual red: app-crap-gate cancelled. Is there any chance the app-crap-gate would FAIL (not cancel) on this PR's code? If yes, pushing without fixing would just go red again (2/3!). That's the real risk to check: the CRAP ratchet on the PR's refactored code with the merged shard coverage.

The PR refactored `_seedBundledSkills` into `_retireSeededCopy` + loops. Let me:
1. Read the current code on the head.
2. Estimate its CC and coverage. CC of `_retireSeededCopy`: branches: try(1) + if body!=null(1) + if !isStale(1) + if leftovers.isOk(1) + && (1) + if empty(1)... roughly CC 6-7. CRAP at coverage c: CC²(1-c) + CC. At c=0 → 49 > 30 threshold! If the new helper is NOT covered by the shard coverage, it'd blow the 30.0 ratchet. But the new test covers it (the test runs in flutter-tests shards and exercises AgentService.create → _seedBundledSkills → _retireSeededCopy with multiple cases). So coverage of this function should be ~100%. But wait — which shard runs skills_toggles_store_test.dart? Both shards run different halves of the test suite; the coverage MERGES both shards (union). So any function covered by ANY test in either shard counts. The CRAP ratchet uses the union — good.

But careful: is `_seedBundledSkills` even executed in widget tests? Yes — the pre-existing tests in skills_toggles_store_test.dart (like 'a fresh env resolves the builtins without any seeded copy') create AgentService with MemoryExecutionEnv, which triggers the seeding path. So `_retireSeededCopy` gets executed. 

However — CRAP counts per-FUNCTION coverage from lcov. The lcov lines for the helper get hit by the new test → cov high → CRAP low. Fine.

But there's a subtlety: `dart pub global run crap4dart analyze` uses lcov + the analyzer's cyclomatic complexity. The old code: `_seedBundledSkills` had 2 loops × (try + if null + if !stale) — CC ~ 11-12? CRAP at 0% could be 132+. But it was covered enough before (threshold 30 held on main with the OLD code — main's head passed the full CI at 20:21, success, including app-crap-gate? main run 37525825919 at 20:21:31 success — that's the push CI on main 34446022c — it would include app-crap-gate since main classifies everything as affected. It succeeded). The PR's refactor REDUCES _seedBundledSkills complexity and adds a small well-covered helper → CRAP strictly improves or stays equal. So the ratchet will pass.

Let me now verify things locally:
1. `dart analyze` / `flutter analyze` on the two changed files (and ideally the flutter_app).
2. Run `flutter test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart` in flutter_app.
3. Possibly run crap4dart analyze with a locally generated lcov — heavy; but there might be a temp flutter SDK from the previous session (flutter-sdk-1156). Let me check.

Also — check AGENTS.md for conventions (it's 124KB; read the relevant sections: maybe a section about rework/validation). Let me search AGENTS.md for "rework" / "red" / "validation" to understand the machine loop expectations.

===
# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): awf main is load-bearing and review-gated, so
    # pack fixes go live on merge with no re-pin ceremony (recently
    # shipped on main: #579 conflict-rework, #577/#578
    # mutexExcludeSelf-by-fact-of-holding, #576 review-machine-unlinked,
    # #573-#574 pack snapshots + registry env, #572 review-stale-verdict,
    # #571 dmtools self-heal, #570 SM budget 1→3, #569 rework fatality,
    # #568 mergeBot workspace/repository args, #566 pack-registry runner
    # overrides). Accepted trade-off: a mutable ref executes whatever
    # sits at the awf main head at run start. The ENGINE (dmtools-agents)
    # resolves from releases via vars — no factory_ref here. Flip in
    # lockstep with the other machine-loop stubs — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

So the red was NOT a test failure or code issue — it was a cancelled job. On re-run (the 20:18 attempt), the CRAP job stayed cancelled (a re-run of failed jobs doesn't re-run cancelled ones, or it was cancelled again by the newer push at 20:20).

My job as the armed rework agent: make sure the PR is in good shape, push if needed (new head resets the red counter), and reply to the thread.

2. But wait — is there anything actually wrong with the code? The CRAP gate cancellation was mechanical (cancelled by concurrency), not a code defect. However, I should verify the PR's own tests still pass on the current head (which includes merges from main). The PR description says "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" got cancelled — that's the flutter_app CRAP ratchet job. There's a `.crap-baseline.json` in repo root. A CRAP ratchet might fail if the new test code increases complexity... but it was cancelled, not failed.

CRAP (Change Risk Anti-Patterns) measures cyclomatic complexity × coverage. Test files usually aren't counted in CRAP baselines (only lib code). The changed lib file is `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_skills.dart`. The refactor collapsed two loops into a helper — that may CHANGE the complexity metrics of the lib file! blocks.text:
# Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them
  # into ONE lcov (union DA hits, never cat — same as the core guards)
  # and runs the pinned crap4dart against flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
  # It is also the only home of the config guards: badge sync (AC1),
  # generated-exclude parity (E1) and the only-down git-history threshold
  # guard (AC3) — a raised threshold cannot merge, a new one (bootstrap)
  # can.
  app-crap-gate:
    name: Flutter app CRAP ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, flutter-tests]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no app/shared changes — flutter_app CRAP green-skipped (required context reported)"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # only-down guard diffs thresholds against the base
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - name: Pub cache (crap4dart)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}
          restore-keys: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: app-coverage-shard-*
          path: app-coverage-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          count=$(ls app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "2" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 2 app shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p flutter_app/coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info \
            app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: Config guards — badge sync, exclude parity, only-down (AC1/E1/AC3)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          [ -n "$BASE_SHA" ] || BASE_SHA=HEAD~1
          python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 (analyzer 14.4 refresh).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 <0.12.0 — same bounded pin as the core job;
          # 0.11.0 carries the Type-2 duplication gate the repo pins to.
          # coverage.run_tests: false in both configs — the merged shard
          # lcov above is the source; never re-run the suite here.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json > crap_report.json

      # Issue #490 AC2: publish the ranked CRAP JSON even when the ratchet
      # is red (analyze writes the report to stdout before its non-zero
      # exit) — descents rank from this artifact, never from a local
      # ad-hoc run.
      - name: Upload crap_report.json artifact (issue 490 AC2)
        if: always() && (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: crap_report
          path: flutter_app/crap_report.json
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Pixel and flutter gates over test/golden/goldens (issue 447)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart check

  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  # duration-balanced manifest (scripts/faui_test_shards.json, rebalanced
  # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml), one file executed by exactly ONE shard,
  # goldens excluded exactly as before (host-locked). Shards fan out INSIDE
  # the job graph; only the aggregate Quality gate is a required check, so
  # a red shard = red gate and path-skipped = neutral (AC4 semantics). A
  # single failed matrix leg can be rerun alone via "Re-run failed jobs"
  # (E1) — the gate then re-aggregates the same results.

The `app-crap-gate` job:
1. Merges the two flutter-test shard coverage reports.

# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.

KEY finding: 

```yaml

  push:
    branches: [main]     # push CI only on main!
  workflow_dispatch: ... # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads: pushes fire NO CI —
  # the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches

  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules)
```

So: pushes to the PR branch fire NO CI. Validation on PR heads is dispatched by the SM (state machine) when "validation is due (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules)". The earlier CI run 37523344821 on the branch at 20:01:52 was such a dispatch (triggered by the SM). It went red on app-crap-gate=cancelled.

Wait — the run's event: let me verify run 37523344821's event was workflow_dispatch. Also the red was on the OLD head 2598bccd9; the head has since moved (merges at 20:20 and 20:27 — from the merge bot "sm-silent-update"). Since pushes fire no CI, validation on the NEW head 1c628d4617 will be dispatched by the SM when due.

Now — "after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head" — red 1/3 on 2598bccd9. The SM's rules: the rework agent is armed (arm 1/2 used?). "🔁 guest rework arm 1/2" means arm 1 of 2 was consumed? This session is presumably arm... hmm, "guest rework arm 1/2" might mean this arming is 1 of max 2.

So what does the SM expect from me (the rework agent)?
1. Investigate the red → done: app-crap-gate leg was cancelled, not failed. No code defect.
2. Fix findings and push → the finding is "validation went red". Since the cause was a cancelled leg (infra), the "fix" is to let validation re-run. A new head already exists (1c628d4617). The SM will dispatch validation on it when due. Do I need to push anything? If the rework pushes (even an empty chore commit), the head changes and validation re-runs fresh. But the guidance also says don't add unrequested commits... The rework contract: "it fixes the findings and pushes; your own push re-runs validation just the same."

Given:
- The PR content is unchanged since my session started; working tree clean at 1c628d4617.
- Validation hasn't run on 1c628d4617 at all yet (dispatch-only).

Hmm, but will the SM dispatch validation on 1c628d4617 automatically? "the SM ... dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules)". A new head (from the merge bot) should make validation due again. The red head was 2598bccd9; the merge bot pushed new heads at 20:20 and 20:27. The SM's red-slot logic: "after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head" — red is 1/3, so validation isn't blocked.

But hold on — why is the rework agent (me) even triggered then? Because when validation went red, the SM armed the rework agent to fix the red. The arm comment says the rework agent fixes findings and pushes. The findings here: none in code — the red was a cancelled leg. The honest rework output: 
- Investigate the red, document the root cause (cancelled app-crap-gate leg; no code defect).
- Verify locally that the PR is green (run the tests: flutter analyze, the changed test file, skills toggles suite, and ideally the CRAP-sensitive surface).
- Push a new head so validation re-runs on a fresh SHA (this also serves as the "fixes the findings and pushes" behavior — the new head re-runs validation).

Wait, should I really push? Let me think about the alternatives:
a) Push nothing; just reply to the thread explaining the red was a cancelled leg and validation will re-dispatch on the current head. Risk: the SM may be waiting specifically for the rework agent's push to re-arm validation ("your own push re-runs validation just the same"). If I don't push and the SM doesn't re-dispatch (because from its view the head is "dirty" — a merge happened), validation could stall. Hmm.

Actually, look at the timeline: head 1c628d4617 was pushed at 20:27:32 by the merge bot (sm-silent-update). If the SM planned to dispatch validation on it, it would have done so or will shortly. The rework run (me) started at 20:30:34 — armed by the red. The directive says "the rework agent is armed on this PR — it fixes the findings and pushes; your own push re-runs validation just the same."

Given the machine loop design, the SAFEST and most contract-conformant action: verify everything locally, then push a new head (e.g., the merge-updated branch is already new — but pushing MY commit creates an even newer head ensuring validation re-dispatch). But what commit? I have no code findings... 

Hmm, wait. Let me re-check whether there are REAL findings I'm missing. The ai-teammate comment is generic ("Validation CI went red"). The actual red: app-crap-gate cancelled. Is there any chance the app-crap-gate would FAIL (not cancel) on this PR's code? If yes, pushing without fixing would just go red again (2/3!). That's the real risk to check: the CRAP ratchet on the PR's refactored code with the merged shard coverage.

The PR refactored `_seedBundledSkills` into `_retireSeededCopy` + loops. Let me:
1. Read the current code on the head.
2. Estimate its CC and coverage. CC of `_retireSeededCopy`: branches: try(1) + if body!=null(1) + if !isStale(1) + if leftovers.isOk(1) + && (1) + if empty(1)... roughly CC 6-7. CRAP at coverage c: CC²(1-c) + CC. At c=0 → 49 > 30 threshold! If the new helper is NOT covered by the shard coverage, it'd blow the 30.0 ratchet. But the new test covers it (the test runs in flutter-tests shards and exercises AgentService.create → _seedBundledSkills → _retireSeededCopy with multiple cases). So coverage of this function should be ~100%. But wait — which shard runs skills_toggles_store_test.dart? Both shards run different halves of the test suite; the coverage MERGES both shards (union). So any function covered by ANY test in either shard counts. The CRAP ratchet uses the union — good.

But careful: is `_seedBundledSkills` even executed in widget tests? Yes — the pre-existing tests in skills_toggles_store_test.dart (like 'a fresh env resolves the builtins without any seeded copy') create AgentService with MemoryExecutionEnv, which triggers the seeding path. So `_retireSeededCopy` gets executed. 

However — CRAP counts per-FUNCTION coverage from lcov. The lcov lines for the helper get hit by the new test → cov high → CRAP low. Fine.

But there's a subtlety: `dart pub global run crap4dart analyze` uses lcov + the analyzer's cyclomatic complexity. The old code: `_seedBundledSkills` had 2 loops × (try + if null + if !stale) — CC ~ 11-12? CRAP at 0% could be 132+. But it was covered enough before (threshold 30 held on main with the OLD code — main's head passed the full CI at 20:21, success, including app-crap-gate? main run 37525825919 at 20:21:31 success — that's the push CI on main 34446022c — it would include app-crap-gate since main classifies everything as affected. It succeeded). The PR's refactor REDUCES _seedBundledSkills complexity and adds a small well-covered helper → CRAP strictly improves or stays equal. So the ratchet will pass.

Let me now verify things locally:
1. `dart analyze` / `flutter analyze` on the two changed files (and ideally the flutter_app).
2. Run `flutter test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart` in flutter_app.
3. Possibly run crap4dart analyze with a locally generated lcov — heavy; but there might be a temp flutter SDK from the previous session (flutter-sdk-1156). Let me check.

Also — check AGENTS.md for conventions (it's 124KB; read the relevant sections: maybe a section about rework/validation). Let me search AGENTS.md for "rework" / "red" / "validation" to understand the machine loop expectations.

===
# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): awf main is load-bearing and review-gated, so
    # pack fixes go live on merge with no re-pin ceremony (recently
    # shipped on main: #579 conflict-rework, #577/#578
    # mutexExcludeSelf-by-fact-of-holding, #576 review-machine-unlinked,
    # #573-#574 pack snapshots + registry env, #572 review-stale-verdict,
    # #571 dmtools self-heal, #570 SM budget 1→3, #569 rework fatality,
    # #568 mergeBot workspace/repository args, #566 pack-registry runner
    # overrides). Accepted trade-off: a mutable ref executes whatever
    # sits at the awf main head at run start. The ENGINE (dmtools-agents)
    # resolves from releases via vars — no factory_ref here. Flip in
    # lockstep with the other machine-loop stubs — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
